title: Extension by zero commutes with $T$
statement:
Let $a\colon\Lambda\to\Lambda'$ be a morphism of commutative condensed rings, with derived
extensions of scalars $T^X$ ([sk-def-sfb-coefficient-change]), let $X$ and $U$ be schemes, and let
$j\colon U\to X$ be an open immersion. The natural isomorphism

$$
T^X\circ D(j_!)\;\cong\;D(j_!)\circ T^U\colon D(\Mod_{\Lambda_U})\longrightarrow
D(\Mod_{\Lambda'_X})
$$

on the unbounded derived categories, with $D(j_!)$ the levelwise extension by zero
([sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek]), is the conjugate ([def-sfb-conjugate-pull-iso]) of the
isomorphism $D(\operatorname{Res}_{a_U})\circ D(j^*)\cong D(j^*)\circ D(\operatorname{Res}_{a_X})$
of [def-sfb-derived-comap-upper-star-iso] along the adjunctions $D(j_!)\dashv D(j^*)$
([sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek], [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property]) and $T\dashv D(\operatorname{Res})$
([sk-def-sfb-derived-extension-of-scalars]). No flatness of $a$ is needed.

proof.text: For each $B=\Lambda,\Lambda'$, [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek] supplies the exact functor $j_!^B$ and the adjunction $j_!^B\dashv j_B^*$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] to $j_!^B$: its termwise cochain functor preserves quasi-isomorphisms and induces $F_B=D(j_!^B)$ with a natural factorization $F_BQ_U^B\cong Q_X^B\mathrm{CoCh}(j_!^B)$. This replaces the inline cycles-and-boundaries argument by the exact-functor lemma. Here $Q_U^B,Q_X^B$ are the cochain localizations defining the unbounded categories, using only that convention of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. The levelwise $G_B=D(j_B^*)$ and its factorization are those already occurring in [def-sfb-derived-comap-upper-star-iso] for $f=j$. No resolution hypothesis is used.

Levelwise functors and their factorizations through cochain localization: Stacks Tag 015F, derived.tex, lemma-right-derived-exact-functor, via lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization.

proof.text: The functor $j_!^B$ is additive because it is exact ([sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek]); $j_B^*$ is additive by [def-sfb-module-upper-star]. Apply clause (a) of [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy] to $j_!^B\dashv j_B^*$. It supplies an adjunction of the termwise cochain functors whose unit and counit are the degreewise sheaf unit and counit. Thus the chain-map equations and the two triangle identities on complexes are supplied by that lemma, rather than proved inline.

source.place: Definition, ambient adjunction input $D(j_!)\dashv D(j^*)$; coefficient-comparisons unit proof, Extension by zero paragraph (main-20261015 sk-def-sfb-coefficient-comparisons.proof.md:31-35). Termwise adjunction of complexes: clause (a) of lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy (Stacks Tag 08BJ, derived.tex, lemma-adjoint-preserve-K-injectives, proof).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-adjunction-localization] to the cochain adjunction from step 2, with $Q_1=Q_U^B$, $Q_2=Q_X^B$, $\bar L=F_B$, $\bar R=G_B$ and the two factorization isomorphisms from step 1. It gives $F_B\dashv G_B$ on the unbounded derived categories. Its unit and counit formulas identify the maps with the localized degreewise unit and counit, and its triangle identities hold on the whole derived categories. This is precisely the ambient levelwise adjunction required by the statement, for each of the two coefficient rings.

source.place: Definition, ambient adjunction input $D(j_!)\dashv D(j^*)$; coefficient-comparisons unit proof, Extension by zero paragraph (main-20261015 sk-def-sfb-coefficient-comparisons.proof.md:31-35). Descent of the adjunction through localization: Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Localization/Adjunction.lean:89,118,125, via lem-sfb-adjunction-localization.

proof.text: Apply [def-sfb-conjugate-pull-iso] with $\mathcal A=D(\Mod_{\Lambda_X})$, $\mathcal B=D(\Mod_{\Lambda'_X})$, $\mathcal A'=D(\Mod_{\Lambda_U})$, and $\mathcal B'=D(\Mod_{\Lambda'_U})$. Set $E_1=T^X$, $E_2=T^U$, $\mathrm{Res}_1=D(\operatorname{Res}_{a_X})$, $\mathrm{Res}_2=D(\operatorname{Res}_{a_U})$, $U_1=F_\Lambda$, $U_2=F_{\Lambda'}$, $L_1=G_\Lambda$ and $L_2=G_{\Lambda'}$. The two coefficient adjunctions are part of [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-change] (equivalently the derived extension/restriction adjunction of [sk-def-sfb-derived-extension-of-scalars]); the two open adjunctions are supplied by steps 1–3. The isomorphism of [def-sfb-derived-comap-upper-star-iso] for $f=j$ is exactly $e:\mathrm{Res}_2L_2\cong L_1\mathrm{Res}_1$. Its conjugate therefore has source $E_1U_1=T^X D(j_!^\Lambda)$ and target $U_2E_2=D(j_!^{\Lambda'})T^U$. Define the comparison in this node to be that conjugate. This specifies the actual natural isomorphism, not merely its existence. All four categories are unbounded, and none of the cited inputs assumes flatness of $a$; hence the construction requires no such hypothesis.
